newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Acacia sees '98 gold output of 440,000 oz.
newsitem.headline: Acacia sees '98 gold output of 440,000 oz.

text.p: Acacia Resources Ltd said on Thursday it projected gold production of about 440,000 ounces in calendar 1998, up from its estimate of 400,000 ounces for 1997.
The estimate was made during an investor briefing by the company's managing director, Michael Folie.
Folie said Acacia was forecasting gold production of 115,000 ounces from its Sunrise Dam mine in Western Australia in 1997, rising to 130,000 ounces in 1998.

A plant upgrade for the company's Brocks Creek and Union Reefs mines in the Northern Territory was expected to lift gold production from the two mines to about 170,000 ounces in 1998 compared to an estimated 130,000 ounces in 1997.
In its June quarter production report released earlier on Thursday, Acacia estimated its year net profit would rise to A$19 million compared to A$7.5 million in 1996.

Folie said Acacia's cash cost of gold production had fallen 27 percent to A$287 per ounce in the June quarter mainly due to the start up of the Sunrise Dam mine in March, which has a cost of production of just A$230 per ounce.
Acacia has forward sales and put options covering 77 percent of its gold reserves being mines, equivalent 1.5 million ounces of gold or about four times its current production level.
The company said the marked-to-market value of hedging contracts at June 30 represented an increased unrealised gain of about A$184 million compared to A$125 million at March 31.
